data.title: JPMorgan Expands Tokenized Money Market Funds To Solana
data.description:
TL;DR: J.P. Morgan Asset Management says qualified U.S. investors can now access MONY and JLTXX tokenized money market funds on Solana through its Morgan Money platform.

J.P. Morgan Asset Management is bringing two of its tokenized money market funds to Solana, extending a traditional cash-management business across another public blockchain.

In an announcement Thursday, the investment manager said qualified U.S. investors can now access My OnChain Net Yield Fund, known as MONY, and the JPMorgan OnChain Liquidity–Token Money Market Fund, JLTXX, on Solana through its Morgan Money platform. Investors can subscribe and redeem through that institutional interface and receive balances represented at blockchain addresses.

Different funds, different investor rules

The two products are not identical forms of digital cash. MONY is a private placement offered under Rule 506(c), with eligibility restrictions for qualifying investors. JLTXX is a U.S.-registered government money market fund structured to serve cash management needs, including those of stablecoin issuers.

Both represent fund interests rather than ordinary deposit balances. J.P. Morgan's disclosures make clear that the funds are not bank accounts or FDIC-insured deposits, and that even products seeking a stable $1 share value can lose money.

That difference is easy to overlook when a token moves through a wallet interface. The blockchain record can make ownership and transfers more programmable; it does not change the underlying fund's investment objectives, regulatory status or redemption restrictions.

Why Solana now?

Institutions experimenting with tokenized assets increasingly operate across more than one chain. A fund that can be subscribed into on multiple networks may be more useful as a liquidity-management instrument, particularly when portfolio and treasury teams hold digital balances in different environments.

J.P. Morgan says adding Solana is intended to let clients access the same fund strategies across the networks where they operate. It is a distribution and settlement expansion, not the creation of two wholly new investment strategies.

The bank's Morgan Money platform remains central to the customer experience. That is significant because professional investors need controls that go beyond seeing a token balance, including eligibility screening, reporting, fund documents and predictable subscriptions and redemptions.

The company published Solana token addresses for both products, but copying a token identifier from social media is not a substitute for using the manager's verified onboarding channel. Token impersonation and lookalike assets remain a risk in on-chain markets.

For Solana, the listing adds another institutional financial product beyond speculative trading. For J.P. Morgan, it tests whether a familiar regulated fund structure can retain its governance while using a wider set of blockchain rails. Actual institutional adoption and transaction volumes, not the announcement alone, will show the importance of that change.

Related Reading: tokenized assets; crypto custody; stablecoins.

data.title: Sparta Capital Ltd. Provides Corporate Update on Reinstatement Review, Financial Statement Corrections and Governance Matters
data.description:
Not for distribution to U.S. Newswire Services or for dissemination in the United States of America. Any failure to comply with this restriction may constitute a violation of U.S. Securities laws

TORONTO, ON / ACCESS Newswire / October 23, 2026 / Sparta Group (TSXV:SAY) (the "Corporation", the "Company", "Sparta Group", "Sparta Capital", "SAY.V" or "Sparta") reports on the status of the ongoing review by the TSX Venture Exchange (the "Exchange") of the Company's application for reinstatement to trading of its common shares and sets out clarifications and corrections to previously disclosed information.

Trading Reinstatement

The Exchange has completed its reinstatement review. The Company's common shares will be reinstated to trading soon.

Current Loans Receivable Clarification

The Company is clarifying the nature and settlement of a balance previously described in its financial statements as a current loan receivable owed by 1123747 B.C. Ltd., a company associated with a director of Re-ECO Tech Electronic Conversions Ltd. ("Re-ECO"), the Company's majority voting-controlled subsidiary. The Company advanced the underlying funds in connection with giving Re-ECO, through its ERS International division, access to the Nano Sorter AI-based recycling and sorting equipment for use in its e-waste processing and IT Asset Disposition operations. The balance was non-interest-bearing and included no interest, foreign exchange, or top-up component. The balance increased from $80,907 September 30, 2025, to $81,420 on December 31, 2025, and to $84,389 on March 31, 2026, because of G Suite subscription fees and legal fees paid by the Company on behalf of 1123747 B.C. Ltd., net of a repayment of $583. On June 30, 2026, the balance was settled in full through the transfer of the Nano Sorter equipment to Re-ECO, and no cash was received by the Company in connection with the settlement. The balance was accordingly reduced to $nil on June 30, 2026, as disclosed in Note 11 to the Company's unaudited condensed interim consolidated financial statements for the three and nine months ended June 30, 2026, filed on SEDAR+ on August 28, 2026 (the "Q3 2026 Interim Statements"). The Consolidated Statement of Cash Flows in the Q3 2026 Interim Statements presented the $84,389 settlement as a source of cash under investing activities. Because no cash was received, that amount should not have been presented as a cash inflow, and will instead be removed from investing activities and disclosed as a non-cash transaction. The recorded balance is correctly stated at $nil. The corrected cash flow presentation, together with note disclosure describing the non-cash settlement of the balance through the transfer of equipment, will be reflected in the Company's audited annual consolidated financial statements for the fiscal year ending September 30, 2026, required to be filed on or before January 28, 2027 under section 4.2(2) of National Instrument 51-102 - Continuous Disclosure Obligations.

Correction to Marketing Expense Disclosure and Related Internal Controls

The Company is correcting a negative (credit) balance of $(65,561) in marketing (business development) expense that appeared in its unaudited condensed interim consolidated financial statements for the six months ended March 31, 2026. The negative balance resulted from the reversal in fiscal 2026 of a commission accrual recorded at September 30, 2025, relating to revenues earned in fiscal 2025 that were not invoiced or paid until fiscal 2026, which accrual was included in business development expense of $155,683 in the Company's audited financial statements for the year ended September 30, 2025. The $(65,561) balance is a net amount, comprising the reversal of the commission accrual in the amount of $65,74, partially offset by $180 of marketing services expense recorded during the six months ended March 31, 2026. The accrual was reversed to avoid double counting when the related commission invoices were received. Commissions for the six months ended March 31, 2026, were, however, still recorded in consulting fees under the Company's prior practice, so no commission expense was recorded in the marketing account to offset the reversal. The Company has since separated commissions paid to parties that generate sales from fees paid to consultants who provide outside expertise, and the year-to-date commissions were reclassified from consulting fees to marketing expense on June 30, 2026. The negative balance was not attributable to new projects or changes in marketing activity. The three-month business development expense of $664,946 for the period ended June 30, 2026, principally reflects that reclassification of year-to-date commission expenses. The cumulative amount of $599,385 for the nine months ended June 30, 2026, is lower than the three-month amount because the accrual reversal reduced the year-to-date balance. Following its annual general meeting on May 21, 2026, the Company constituted a new Audit Committee (described below) that reviews the Company's quarterly financial statements prior to filing, and the Company has implemented additional review procedures for expense coding, related-party identification and TSXV filing requirements to reduce the risk of similar classification errors recurring.

Disclosure Regarding Share Issuances Prior to Receipt of Funds

In connection with a September 2017 convertible debenture financing, related receipts recorded in 2018, and a 2023 financing, the Company issued common shares prior to receiving, or without ultimately receiving, the related funds in full.

Following closing of the Company's 2023 private placement, subscription receivables totaling $99,500 were outstanding, comprising $79,500 relating to the 2023 private placement and $20,000 carried forward from the earlier financing records. Of the $79,500 relating to the 2023 private placement: (i) $25,000 was collected on January 15, 2024 from ERS International; (ii) $30,000 was owed by Alyn Patterson, the Company's Chief Financial Officer at the time, who was issued 1,000,000 common shares for which payment was not received, an amount disclosed as a related-party amount due from the Chief Financial Officer in the Company's annual filings for fiscal 2023, 2024 and 2025; and (iii) $24,500 was not received. The $20,000 balance traces to a $365,000 convertible debenture financing completed in September 2017. The historical records initially described $75,000 as receivable and subsequently recorded $85,000 as a receivable under "conversion of debentures"; $65,000 was collected between October and December 2018 and recorded as private-placement proceeds, although no shares were issued for that receipt. The remaining $74,500, being $30,000, $24,500 and $20,000, was written off by the Company as uncollectible and recorded as bad debt expense. All common shares issued in respect of the written-off receivables remain issued and outstanding. The share issuance records for these financings were administered by the Company's former President prior to his death in October 2023 and were not fully transferred to current management. The Company has reviewed the available transfer-agent, subscription and payment records and will continue to reconcile the historical accounting entries as additional predecessor-management records become available.

The Company has adopted the practice, effective for all issuances going forward, that it will not issue, or characterize as issued or pending in connection with a financing, common shares until (i) in the case of a private placement, applicable subscription funds have been received and cleared, in accordance with TSX Venture Exchange Policy 4.1 - Private Placements; or (ii) in the case of a debt settlement or services-based issuance, the news release announcing the issuance expressly discloses that the shares are issued for non-cash consideration and does not characterize the transaction as a "private placement," in accordance with TSX Venture Exchange Policy 4.3 - Shares for Debt. As additional remedial and corrective measures, the Company has designated its Chief Financial Officer as responsible for confirming that subscription funds have been received and cleared before instructing the Company's transfer agent to issue any shares in connection with a private placement, and the Company's Audit Committee will review share issuance records, including any outstanding subscription receivables, as part of its quarterly review of the Company's financial statements.

Clarification of October 2, 2024, Private Placement ($102,030)

The Company is correcting the characterization of the transaction announced in its news release dated October 2, 2024, in the amount of $102,030. That amount reflected the aggregate deemed value of common shares issued by the Company in October 2024, and did not represent cash proceeds raised by way of a private placement, as follows: (i) 2,601,510 common shares (together with 2,601,510 warrants exercisable at $0.10 per share for eighteen months) issued at a deemed value of $52,030 (comprising $50,000 principal and $2,030 accrued interest) to Gerald T. Miller in settlement of outstanding debt; and (ii) 2,500,000 common shares (together with 2,500,000 warrants exercisable at $0.10 per share for eighteen months) issued at a deemed value of $50,000 to Advisir Ventures Ltd. for advertising-related services. The Company's October 2, 2024, news release stated that proceeds would be used to fund audit, legal and licence fees; the Company is clarifying that no cash proceeds were received in connection with these share issuances, and that the previously disclosed use of proceeds does not apply to this transaction. Mr. Miller is the Company's external legal counsel; he has never been a director or officer of the Company and does not hold more than 10% of the Company's voting shares. Advisir Ventures Ltd. is an unrelated, arm's-length party to the Company.

Catch-Up Regulatory Filings

In connection with the reinstatement review, the Company confirms that it has made or submitted the following filings to the Exchange:

  • Convertible Debentures: a historical Form 4B filing and supplemental submission under TSX Venture Exchange Policy 4.1 in respect of the Company's outstanding 8% unsecured convertible debentures. The original financing was announced by news releases dated November 3, 2021, and December 3, 2021, and an extension was announced by news release dated January 14, 2022. Between November 2021 and February 2022, the Company issued 55 unsecured convertible debentures at a price of $5,000 per debenture for aggregate gross proceeds of $275,000. Each debenture bore interest at 8% per annum, matured two years from its date of issuance and was convertible into units at $0.20 per unit, with each unit consisting of one common share and one-half of one common share purchase warrant. On October 5, 2022, the Company extended the conversion period and modified the conversion terms for $200,000 face value of existing debentures and issued an additional $150,000 face value of debentures convertible at $0.05 per share until October 5, 2023. In February 2023, a $20,000 debenture was converted into 666,667 common shares. In September 2023, one debenture was increased from $100,000 to $200,000 and the maturity dates of all outstanding debentures were extended to November 2024, resulting in $355,000 of principal outstanding. No separate news releases were identified for the October 2022 changes or the September 2023 amendment. The October 2022 changes and the September amendment have been submitted to the Exchange as part of the Company's catch-up filings and remain subject to Exchange acceptance. The debentures matured in November 2024 and are currently in default and classified as current liabilities. The conversion rights and related warrant entitlements have expired. Consistent with subsection 1.6(h)(ii) of Form 51-102F1, the Company has updated the liquidity risk disclosure in its MD&A to reflect the default status of the debentures. The Company is actively exploring restructuring options, and any future restructuring, extension, refinancing or settlement of the debentures will be submitted to the Exchange for acceptance, as required.
  • Disposition of the Sold Entities: a submission under section 3.1 of TSX Venture Exchange Policy 5.3 - Acquisitions and Dispositions of Non-Cash Assets, addressing the Company's September 30, 2025, disposition of its interests in six non-operating subsidiaries to 2420604 Ontario Limited for aggregate consideration of $5, together with the related threshold analysis.The subsidiaries were non-operational and were generating ongoing administrative expenses to maintain. The Company disposed of them to eliminate those costs and liabilities of the subsidiaries and recognized a one-time gain of disposal. The disposition was unanimously approved by the Company's board of directors, then comprised of Tony Peticca, Shawn Leon and Peter Quattro. Gerald T. Miller, the Company's external legal counsel, is the sole shareholder, director and officer of 2420604 Ontario Limited. Mr. Miller has never been an officer or director of the Company, and Mr. Miller and 2420604 Ontario Limited are arm's-length parties to the Company. The disposition remains subject to acceptance by the Exchange
  • Disposition of Re-ECO: a submission under section 3.1 of TSX Venture Exchange Policy 5.3 addressing the Company's February 3, 2025, disposition of 120,000 Class B Special Shares of Re-ECO, representing 12 percentage points of the Company's equity interest in Re-ECO (reducing the Company's equity interest from 20% to 8%), to 1123747 B.C. Ltd. for cash consideration of $250,000. The disposition was undertaken as part of a corporate realignment and to provide working capital and was unanimously approved by the Company's board of directors, then comprised of Tony Peticca, Shawn Leon and Peter Quattro. The disposition of the Re-ECO Class B Special Shares remains subject to acceptance by the Exchange. 1123747 B.C. Ltd. represents the persons associated with the original business that had the core expertise in electronic recycling and has no relationship to Sparta or any director, officer or other insider of Sparta other than as a co-shareholder of Re-ECO. It is accordingly an arm's-length party to the Company. The disposition involved only Re-ECO's non-voting Class B Special Shares; the Company's holding of Re-ECO's voting Common Class A shares, which carries the Company's controlling voting interest in Re-ECO, was not affected by the transaction. The Company holds 600 of the 1,000 issued and outstanding Common Class A shares of Re-ECO, which are the only voting shares of Re-ECO, representing 60% of the votes attached to all Re-ECO's voting shares, and accordingly retained its 60% voting interest in, and continued to consolidate, Re-ECO following the disposition. On December 12, 2025, Re-ECO separately redeemed 31,000 Class B Special Shares held by the Company for consideration of $150,000, reducing the Company's holding to 48,400 of the 968,000 issued and outstanding Class B Special Shares (approximately 5.0%); the redemption did not affect the Company's voting interest. The proceeds were used to fund the audit and to pay professional fees and operating obligations. Re-ECO is not a reporting issuer in any jurisdiction, there is no published market for its Class B Special Shares, and those shares are held by fewer than 50 holders; the redemption was accordingly exempt from the issuer bid requirements of National Instrument 62-104 - Take-Over Bids and Issuer Bids under section 4.9 thereof. Because Re-ECO is not listed on the Exchange, TSX Venture Exchange Policy 5.5 does not apply to the redemption;
  • Shares for Debt: a shares-for-debt application under TSX Venture Exchange Policy 4.3 (Submission #SUB-743746) in respect of $619,167 of bona fide indebtedness for consulting and management services owed to seven creditors, to be settled through the issuance of 30,958,350 common shares at a deemed price of $0.02 per share. The indebtedness comprises $310,000 for services rendered in the year ended September 30, 2024, and $309,167 for services rendered in the year ended September 30, 2025. The fiscal 2024 obligations were originally included in accounts payable and accrued liabilities as of September 30, 2024, and were reclassified during fiscal 2025 to common shares to be issued. The fiscal 2025 obligations were recorded as consulting fees with a corresponding credit to common shares to be issued. The aggregate $619,167 is disclosed in Note 10 to the Company's financial statements as common shares to be issued and is not included in current liabilities as of June 30, 2026. The creditors are: Tony Peticca, President and a director (9,500,000 shares); Shawn Leon, Chief Executive Officer and a director (5,500,000 shares); Peter Quattro, Chairman and a director (1,000,000 shares); Gerald T. Miller, the Company's external legal counsel (9,000,000 shares); Taylor O'Bireck (4,500,000 shares); Marty Marshall, a former director (500,000 shares); and Joseph Cimorelli, a former director (958,350 shares). This amount excludes the Company's separate 2026 compensation arrangement with director Edward Vranic, which will be addressed under a separate filing when applicable. Because shares are being issued to non-arm's-length parties, the transaction requires disinterested shareholder approval under section 6.3 of TSX Venture Exchange Policy 4.4. The Company intends to seek disinterested shareholder approval of the transaction at its next annual general meeting of shareholders, and votes attached to common shares held by the non-arm's-length creditors participating in the transaction and their associates and affiliates will be excluded from that approval. Completion of the transaction remains subject to receipt of disinterested shareholder approval and final acceptance of the Exchange, and the terms of the transaction, including the deemed price and number of shares to be issued, may be subject to adjustment as required by the Exchange.

Annual General Meeting, Board and Audit Committee Update

The Company held its annual general meeting on May 21, 2026, at which shareholders elected Keith Whann, Ralph Goldsilver, Philip Chen and Edward Vranic to the Company's board of directors, joining continuing directors Tony Peticca, Shawn Leon and Peter Quattro. Immediately following the annual general meeting, the board of directors held its first meeting, at which Shawn Leon was appointed Chief Executive Officer of the Company, Peter Quattro (the Company's former Chief Executive Officer) was appointed Chairman of the Board, and a new Audit Committee was constituted, comprised of Ralph Goldsilver (independent), Keith Whann (independent) and Shawn Leon (non-independent, by virtue of his position as Chief Executive Officer), consistent with the venture-issuer exemptions available under section 6.1 of National Instrument 52-110 - Audit Committees.

Additional Disclosure - Continued Listing Requirements

The Company does not currently meet the working capital criterion of the Exchange's Continued Listing Requirements. Based on the Company's unaudited condensed interim consolidated financial statements as of June 30, 2026, the Company has a working capital deficiency of $137,848 and does not meet the Exchange's six-month general and administrative expense requirement of approximately $4,612,000.

The Company intends to address its working capital deficiency and work toward satisfying the Exchange's Continued Listing Requirements through a combination of operating performance and new financing. The Company's working capital position has fluctuated with the cyclical nature of ERS International's recycling and IT asset disposition business and has improved significantly from the position that existed when trading was suspended. The Company returned to profitability in fiscal 2025. Although ERS International's revenue and profitability declined in fiscal 2026, the expenses incurred during that period included investments made in anticipation of a return to profitable growth in fiscal 2027, which management expects to have a positive impact on the Company's working capital position. Following the resumption of trading, the Company also intends to pursue an equity financing at the corporate level, separate from ERS International, targeting gross proceeds of approximately $500,000 to $1,500,000. The final size, pricing, structure and timing of the financing have not been determined and will be subject to market conditions and applicable regulatory approvals and Exchange acceptance. The Company has had preliminary discussions with prospective investors and has received non-binding expressions of interest, but no definitive subscription agreements or other commitments have been entered into. If completed, the Company expects to use the net proceeds to provide working capital and fund ongoing corporate operations and growth initiatives. The Company also intends to complete the proposed shares-for-debt transaction described in item (f) above and to explore a restructuring, extension, refinancing or settlement of the $355,000 convertible debentures in each case subject to required shareholder approval and Exchange acceptance. There can be no assurance that the Company will complete any financing or other measure, or that it will meet the Continued Listing Requirements, and if it does not, the Exchange may transfer the Company's listing to the NEX board or take other action under its policies.

About Sparta Capital Ltd.

Sparta Capital Ltd. is a publicly traded company listed on the TSX Venture Exchange under the symbol "SAY." The Company operates through a decentralized structure with active business units in two primary verticals: Environmental Services, through ERS International (a division of Re-ECO Tech Electronic Conversions Ltd.), which provides e-waste processing, IT Asset Disposition and related environmental services; and Health Technology, through Sparta Health Corporation's Doc-in-a-Box clinician-facing advisory and decision-support platform.

data.title: Will Anthropic pull off a November IPO? Time is running out to file key paperwork.
data.description:
By William Gavin

If market pressures keep building, Anthropic 'could reasonably decide it is better to stay private and wait for a better opportunity,' one portfolio manager says

Anthropic, which makes the Claude suite of products, is one of the pillars of the AI boom.

Anthropic may be just days away from making a major step toward becoming a public company - but there's still time for things to change.

The company is one of the biggest pillars of the artificial-intelligence industry, and its anticipated initial public offering is likely to reinforce that. Anthropic is reportedly seeking a valuation of as much as $2 trillion, which could result in an even more explosive IPO than SpaceX's (SPCX) $1.77 trillion debut earlier this year.

According a Reuters report on Thursday, the Claude chatbot maker plans to hold its IPO in the middle of November, which means time is running out to file some important paperwork. The U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission requires a company to publicly file its prospectus at least 15 days before it launches a roadshow.

Jay Ritter, who leads the University of Florida's IPO Initiative, told MarketWatch that Anthropic has some time if it still wants to go public before Thanksgiving. If the company were to hold its IPO as late as Nov. 24 and start its roadshow with investors on Nov. 16, Anthropic would have until late next week to publicly file its S-1 document, he said.

However, it's also possible that Anthropic decides to push back its IPO. The company was once expected to publicly unveil its IPO prospectus shortly after Labor Day, which could have set the stage for it to list later in September. Experts say it's likely, but not certain, that Anthropic will still want to make a debut now.

Anthropic did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

The market has become less hospitable to AI companies lately, which is one factor that could give pause to Anthropic's management team. Joe Tigay, a portfolio manager at the Rational Equity Armor Fund HDCAX, told MarketWatch that persistent inflation and high energy prices could also be cause for concern.

"Historically, that combination of slowing growth and persistent inflation can be where stock markets crack. If those pressures keep building, Anthropic could reasonably decide it is better to stay private and wait for a better opportunity," Tigay told MarketWatch over email.

But the market needs a successful Anthropic IPO to prove that AI has staying power, argued Jim Lebenthal, chief market strategist at Cerity Partners. He noted that the longevity and economics of the AI industry have been further called into question recently.

Shares of the neocloud company CoreWeave (CRWV), for example, have dropped roughly 30% over the last two weeks on concerns about the company's ability to manage its debt. Even companies that are swimming in cash have been swept up in the downward action. Micron Technology's stock (MU) has lost 17% over the past month against the broader backdrop of fears over AI spending and financing.

"It's reasonable to have questions. It's reasonable even to have doubts," Lebenthal said. "But the health of the overall equity market and the health of the U.S. economy relies vitally on the artificial-intelligence industry being successful."

Of course, Anthropic's reasons for going public wouldn't be to buoy stock-market sentiment toward AI. Simply put, Anthropic needs the cash, according to Andrew Rocco, a stock strategist at Zacks Investment Research.

The biggest AI companies have shown that "they're basically willing to spend as much as they can in order to capture more customers and try and be the dominant AI player," Rocco told MarketWatch. "In my view they're going to try and get this out because they do need that capital, especially since it's going to be probably harder to just raise it in the private market."

Anthropic could spend as much as $750 billion on AI compute capacity in the coming years, according to the Wall Street Journal, which cited a copy of its draft IPO prospectus. The Journal also noted that Anthropic recorded a net loss of more than $80 billion in the first half of 2026 against revenue of $16.3 billion, though the loss was largely driven by accounting adjustments rather than fundamental business developments.

Rocco noted that prediction markets show an 80% chance of the company going public by the end of the year.

-William Gavin

data.title: Morocco expects stable fiscal deficit despite tax cuts in 2027
data.description:
By Ahmed Eljechtimi

Morocco expects a steady fiscal deficit at 3% of GDP despite higher spending on social programmes and tax cuts, newly appointed finance and economy minister Fouzi Lekjaa said on Friday.

The economy is expected to grow 3.7% in 2027, down from a forecast of 4.7% this year, assuming an average crop year, Lekjaa told members of parliament while presenting the 2027 draft budget.

Morocco announced a new government coalition last week following September 23 elections, placing priority on purchasing power, social services and youth employment, one year after GenZ protests and the Ceuta migration crisis in July.

The government's social policies in previous years have been weakened by an economic model that prioritised market forces over regulation, fostering monopolistic practices, rent-seeking and quick profits, Lekjaa said.

"Savage capitalism and neo-liberalism" have been at the heart of social tension, he said, urging a stronger role for the state in combating corruption, conflicts of interest and monopolies, while safeguarding food and energy sovereignty.

In total, the government plans to spend 62 billion dirhams ($6.3 billion) next year on measures aimed at improving social services, boosting purchasing power and reducing inequalities, Lekjaa said.

The measures include reforming distribution channels for basic goods, promoting youth employment and exempting salaries of less than 10,000 dirhams a month, which would account for 87% of all employees, from income tax, he said.

The package also includes pension increases, higher financial aid for needy families and electricity subsidies.

The health budget would rise 7% to 45.5 billion dirhams, while education spending would increase 4.6% to 121 billion dirhams, according to the draft budget.

The draft also authorises defence expenditure commitments of up to 190.5 billion dirhams.

Public debt is forecast to decline to 66.9% of GDP in 2027 from 67.5% this year, the budget document showed.

The government proposes raising to 40% the tax rate on profits above 100 million dirhams earned by fuel distribution companies, a sector previously sanctioned by competition authorities for anti-competitive practices.

The draft budget increases excise taxes on soft drinks, alcoholic beverages, cigarettes and e-cigarettes.

The government's financing requirement is expected to fall 7.4% to 159 billion dirhams in 2027 as it seeks to balance domestic and external borrowing "depending on market conditions," according to the draft budget.

data.title: France spared Moody's ratings downgrade as it struggles with unrest
data.description:
Key points:
  • Moody's leaves France rating at Aa3 with a negative outlook
  • S&P and Fitch have already cut France

By Leigh Thomas and Dhara Ranasinghe

Moody's spared France a credit rating downgrade on Friday, easing pressure on a government struggling to contain social unrest and shore up its strained finances.

Moody's said it had concluded a periodic review of its rating, leaving it at Aa3, which has carried a negative outlook since last October.

Bond markets had been pricing in a downgrade, which would have brought Moody's in line with Standard & Poor's and Fitch, which moved earlier as France struggled to rein in its public finances after a 2024 snap election produced a hung parliament and political paralysis.

The French finance ministry said in a statement that the fact Moody's kept its rating unchanged reflected the "credibility of the budget the government has put forward in the 2027 finance bill, which is designed to keep our public finances on the path to recovery."

The government is struggling to pass the bill in parliament, where opposition parties could refuse to compromise, reject the legislation and topple the government in a no-confidence vote.

"The Aa3 rating assumes that a deficit-reducing budget for 2027 will be adopted, while financing costs and social tensions will abate somewhat in the next few months," Moody's said in a statement.

French borrowing costs already exceed those of lower-rated peers such as Italy, as investors fret over the budget deficit — one of the euro zone's biggest — and a presidential election on April 18 and May 2 next year that polls suggest the far right could win.

TV images of weekend protests descending into riots and looting underscore the political difficulty of pushing budget cuts through.

That helped push the risk premium on French government debt over safe-haven German bonds to its highest in 15 years on Thursday, while France's benchmark 10-year bond yield hit 5.14%, its highest level since July 2002.

OUTLOOK IN FOCUS

Moody's said earlier this month that the French government's ability to overcome "fragmentation in parliament" would be the key factor for its next rating move.

That task looks harder after violent protests over underfunded schools escalated last weekend into riots during mass cost-of-living demonstrations. The government has refused to release more school funding or raise the minimum wage, and further protests are planned for Saturday.

In parliament, the lower house has scrapped some key savings measures in the 2027 budget, which targets a deficit of 5% of output versus 5.4% this year. Opposition parties show little appetite for compromise before the election, scrapping some proposed cuts while adding spending.

"You want to wait and see how the narrative evolves over the next six months into the election. That's going to have a more meaningful impact on the spread," said Rushabh Amin, a portfolio manager at Allspring Global Investments.

Pressure on French debt could grow after the presidential vote if Moody's, S&P and Fitch all cut France to BBB — just above junk status — potentially forcing sales by those investors with rating limits, said Mike Bell, head of market strategy at RBC BlueBay Asset Management.

"That's where it could really start to get more ugly," he added.

BETHESDA, Md., Oct. 23, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Elme Communities (“Elme” or the “Company”) today announced that the New York Stock Exchange (“NYSE”) has exercised its discretionary authority in accordance with Section 802.01D of the NYSE Listed Company Manual to commence proceedings to delist Elme’s common shares of beneficial interest (the “Common Shares”) from the NYSE due to “abnormally low selling price” levels. The NYSE also immediately suspended trading of the Common Shares. Given the Company’s previously adopted Plan of Sale and Liquidation (as defined below), Elme does not intend to appeal the NYSE’s determination, and, therefore, it is expected that the Common Shares will be delisted.

The Company anticipates the Common Shares will commence trading over-the-counter (“OTC”) on Monday, October 26, 2026 under the symbol “ELMES”. There can be no assurance regarding the development or maintenance of an active OTC trading market or the liquidity of any such market. Investors are cautioned that trading securities OTC is more limited and subject to different restrictions than trading securities listed on a national securities exchange and are advised to consult their own brokers or advisors.

Anticipated Timing of Establishment of a Liquidating Trust and Company Dissolution

As previously disclosed, in accordance with the Plan of Sale and Liquidation approved by the Board of Trustees (the “Board”) on July 30, 2025 and by the shareholders of the Company on October 30, 2025 (the “Plan of Sale and Liquidation”), it is the Company’s continued intention to terminate its existence by voluntary dissolution effective November 6, 2026 (the “Effective Time”), which will occur following the NYSE’s delisting of our Common Shares. In addition, as previously disclosed, the Company expects that its share transfer books will close at the close of business (Eastern Time) on November 5, 2026.

Prior to the Effective Time, the Company intends to transfer all of its remaining assets and liabilities to a Maryland liquidating trust (the “Liquidating Trust”). The purpose of the Liquidating Trust will be to liquidate the remaining assets (which are expected to consist primarily of the net cash proceeds from property sales) of the Liquidating Trust and distribute the amounts remaining in the Liquidating Trust, if any, after satisfaction of all remaining liabilities (including any additional liabilities, costs and expenses that may arise during the wind-down process) to the holders of the beneficial interests of the Liquidating Trust (the “Beneficial Interests”) upon completion of the wind-down process and in connection with termination of the Liquidating Trust. All of the Beneficial Interests will be held by the shareholders of the Company, with each shareholder of the Company being deemed automatically to have received and hold a percentage of Beneficial Interests in the Liquidating Trust corresponding to such shareholder’s percentage ownership in the Company as of the close of business on the last day of trading of the Common Shares. Shareholders of the Company will not be required to take any action to receive Beneficial Interests in the Liquidating Trust. The actual amount and timing of payment of any additional liquidating distribution(s) from the Liquidating Trust will be determined by the trustee of the Liquidating Trust in their sole discretion. As previously disclosed, the Company expects FTI Consulting, Inc. to be retained to provide services in connection with completing the wind-down process, including the services of a liquidating trustee to serve as trustee of the Liquidating Trust.

Following the transfer of the Company’s assets and liabilities to the Liquidating Trust, subject to certain exceptions related to transfer by will, intestate succession or operation of law, Beneficial Interests in the Liquidating Trust will not be transferable, nor will holders of Beneficial Interests have authority or power to sell or in any other manner dispose of their Beneficial Interests. However, the Corporation expects that the aggregate fair market value of all Colt Shares distributed pursuant to the Share Exchange under the Arrangement will not exceed the aggregate PUC of the Palamina Shares. data.title: PHP Foundation 'under-funded' with one full-time staff member, director says
data.description:
Key points:
  • Funding comes from donations and grants
  • AI-related increase in coding has doubled foundation's workload
  • No evidence seen of vulnerabilities' pre-disclosure exploitation

By Toby Sterling

The discovery of two serious flaws in PHP this week set off a global scramble to keep websites safe from hackers, showing just how critical the three-decade-old open-source programming language is to the internet.

Yet the nonprofit foundation that supports PHP, which may underpin up to 70% of sites globally, operates on a shoestring budget.

“We have one full-time staff member (that's me) and 14 mostly part-time contractors,” Executive Director Elizabeth Barron of the PHP Foundation said via email in an interview on Friday. Board members are unpaid volunteers, and funding comes from donations and grants.

The foundation works with outside researchers and companies, including OpenAI and cybersecurity firms Wiz and Calif, to investigate security flaws and coordinate fixes, including Wednesday's patches.

While Web security company Cloudflare has reported millions of hacking attempts, Barron said the foundation had no evidence hackers were able to exploit the vulnerabilities before they were disclosed, or on sites that have been patched.

"We received no further indication from OpenAI, Wiz or Calif, with whom we're working closely on this issue, regarding any issues on patched systems,” she said.

Artificial intelligence has proved both a help and a burden to the foundation. It helped researchers find the flaws, which had been present for a decade, and Barron said it made programmers more efficient.

However, it is also increasing maintainers' workloads. The PHP project is receiving nearly twice as many proposed code changes as a year ago, “yet the number of contributors hasn't doubled,” she said. Reviewing contributions and bug reports requires “a massive amount of human input and experience.”

Recent events have shown how heavily companies and governments rely on PHP, Barron said.

“Given that reliance, it is clear that PHP is incredibly under-funded.”
